page.summary: Buy repair time by lasting in chase, then return to objectives when the Killer will not take the chase you want.

verdict.recommendation: Build for extending a chase, not for spending the whole Trial trying to attract one.
verdict.soloQ: The Solo loadout keeps post-unhook protection alongside chase tools, since nobody can promise to cover you.
verdict.coordinatedSwf: Agree where teammates are repairing and take pressure away from that work; a runner's time matters only if the team uses it.
verdict.mainWeakness: The Killer can ignore you, and the usable resources on your route do not last forever.

notes.whyItsHere: Use the vault exit to reach the next resource rather than exhausting one loop without a follow-up.
Help your route continue after a hit; the value is in surviving the next decision, not deliberately remaining in danger.
Support the opening healthy part of a chase. Plan a different margin once you are injured or the perk is resting.
Keep an answer to a repeat pickup after an unhook rather than investing every slot in a chase the Killer can refuse.
Choose one tool whose availability fits your route and the team's plan.

optionReasons.whyItsHere: Choose this to start the escape toward a usable tile when pressure reaches your position; do not let saving it stop you doing objectives.
Choose this for a later injured chase after an unhook, when you can judge the incoming attack. It is not a substitute for an opening escape before you have been unhooked.

notes.whyItsHere: Support a healthy runner's fast-vault route while keeping its availability separate from injured chase tools.
Keep some vault and interaction value after the runner takes a hit, when the healthy-vault tool no longer covers the route.
Identify an available pallet route under pressure and leave decisively after a drop. Do not read this as window information or an always-available movement bonus.

opening: Identify a first resource and an onward route while doing objectives. With teammates on voice, check which generator area should stay clear of your chase.

rows.situation: You are approaching a fast vault while healthy, or have just taken a hit on that route.
rows.action: Check whether Finesse is available for the healthy vault. After a hit, reassess the next loop using your injured-state tools and remaining resources instead of repeating the same tight vault.
rows.why: Finesse and Resilience cover different health states; equipping both does not make every vault doubly protected.

rows.situation: You are using the Solo loadout and a rushed vault can lead to another usable tile.
rows.action: Commit to that onward route with Lithe available. If Exhausted, plan the transition without expecting the burst.
rows.why: A planned exit extends the chase more reliably than activating mobility with nowhere safe to run.

rows.situation: Pressure reaches you while using the coordinated loadout.
rows.action: With Sprint Burst available, start the escape toward your chosen resource. With Dead Hard chosen, rely on normal routing until its post-unhook injured-chase conditions are met, then judge the attack rather than pressing it automatically.
rows.why: The two options solve different moments; choosing one does not give you the other one's opening.

rows.situation: You are under pressure with Five Moves Ahead available.
rows.action: Pick a pallet that leads somewhere useful. After dropping it, use the exit to move on and remember the tool is now on cooldown.
rows.why: Pallet information supports a route; spending a pallet just to trigger the perk spends the route's future safety.

rows.situation: You have been unhooked while using the Solo loadout and are being pursued again.
rows.action: Stay focused on escape and check Will to Live's availability before counting on a pickup opportunity. If you have resumed Conspicuous Actions or the gates are powered, route without that insurance.
rows.why: A conditional safety tool cannot justify taking a down for the sake of extending your assigned runner role.

rows.situation: The Killer leaves you or will not pursue you.
rows.action: Repair or cover the needed rescue instead of following the Killer to demand another chase. In a group, call the target switch so the next player can route early.
rows.why: Unused chase perks are a sunk cost; ordinary objective work still advances the Trial.

abortWhen: If the next tile has no usable resource, stop repeating the old loop and take the best remaining route before the Killer closes it.
When teammates need a rescue more than another distraction, drop the runner assignment and cover the actual need.

soloQ: Do not assume a long chase means teammates are repairing; once released, check which job is actually uncovered.
coordinatedSwf: Call where you are taking chase and where pallets have been spent. Teammates should keep the agreed objectives moving instead of all shadowing the runner.

weaknesses: Chase value depends on the resources and routes still available; a depleted area cannot be repaired by adding more chase perks.
killerCounterplay: The Killer can refuse the runner, switch to a less prepared teammate or force resources out of the route before committing again.
commonMistakes: Treating healthy and injured perk bonuses as though they apply at the same time.
Using a pallet for its perk payoff without planning the next tile.
Keeping the Killer's attention at the cost of bringing pressure directly onto the team's repair work.
